To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the metabolite–protein interaction network is an excellent resource for closing the gap between therapeutic use and mode of action of remedial herbs, and that this network can be used to generate hypotheses on mode of action of such plants.
a network-based approach to integrate metabolite, protein, and disease knowledge is able to generate plausible mode of action hypotheses to support the therapeutic use of remedial herbs.

a mechanistic hypothesis can be generated when a metabolites, plant, disease, and protein are connected by a chain of interactions, and that a mechanistic explanation for the therapeutic use of a plant can be generated if the disease can be connected to the function of the protein and the protein can be predicted or experimentally confirmed to interact with the metabolite.

closing the gap between therapeutic uses and mode of action in remedial herbs by connecting metabolites, plant species, diseases, and protein functions.
